## The Spectacular Elan Valley

### 70 square miles of dams, reservoirs and rugged Welsh landscapes.

There’s plenty to see and do in the Elan Valley. By day, explore this special landscape by bike, car or on foot. When the sun sets and the night falls, look up and marvel at the star-studded skies.

Come and explore this magical place, nestled in the heart of the Cambrian Mountains of Mid Wales.

# A visitor's guide to Elan Valley

Whatever your interest, whatever time of year, you can always have a Mid Wales adventure in Cwm Elan (Elan Valley). With spectacular dams and scenery, it's one of Wales' most picturesque spots.

SaveShare

Cwm Elan in rural Mid Wales has been inspiring visitors for centuries. Inhabited since the Stone Age, the area became known for mining, religious sites and for taking part in the [Rebecca Riots](http://history.powys.org.uk/history/rhaeadr/rebecca.html) of the 1840s. Today the valley is famous for the spectacular dams and scenery. The nearest large town is Rhaeadr Gwy (Rhayader), on [The Cambrian Way](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3091) snaking through Mid Wales.

Over 80% of the valley is designated as [Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI)](https://www.elanvalley.org.uk/discover/nature), home to reservoirs, aqueducts, hundreds of animals and loads of opportunities to have fun. We’ve put together a few suggestions on how to have a truly memorable and adventurous time in the beautiful Cwm Elan.

## Elan Valley dams and reservoirs

The dams and reservoirs were built to supply regular fresh water to Birmingham. Building work began in 1883, continuing until the last dam was opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1953. There are six impressive [dams](https://elan-valley.co.uk/history-and-the-elan-valley-dams/) altogether. Four follow the Elan River - [Craig Goch](https://elan-valley.co.uk/craig-goch/), [Pen y Garreg](https://elan-valley.co.uk/pen-y-garreg/), [Garreg Ddu](https://elan-valley.co.uk/garreg-ddu/), and [Caban Coch](https://elan-valley.co.uk/caban-coch/) and two are on the river Claerwen - the [Claerwen dam](https://elan-valley.co.uk/claerwen/) and the unfinished [Dol y Mynach](https://elan-valley.co.uk/dol-y-mynach/) dam.

## How to get there

The easiest way to get there by car is to head to Rhaeadr Gwy, at the crossroads of the A44 from the east or the A470 from North or South Wales. Follow the B4518 to the west then look out for signposts towards the [Elan Valley Visitor Centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/917601).

Rhayader is easy to get to by public transport - [Traveline Cymru](https://www.traveline.cymru/) can help. It's around three miles to the Visitor Centre so you can walk if you're feeling active or pre-book a taxi with a local firm. Cyclists can follow the [Lon Cambria](https://www.sustrans.org.uk/find-a-route-on-the-national-cycle-network/lon-cambria-aberystwyth-to-shrewsbury/?./lon-cambria-and-lon-teifi?&_suid=137543800213809154257409454448) trail which takes you right into the heart of Cwm Elan.

## What to do around Elan Valley

### Bike and hike

With open access to most of the 72 square mile [Elan Valley estate](https://elan-valley.co.uk/), there are so many routes you can take to explore the area. Whether you want a gentle stroll through the greenery and dams or a more challenging hike amongst rocky crags and waterways, there will be a route to suit your needs and ability. [Bike hire](https://elan-valley.co.uk/cycling/) is readily available, if you fancy seeing the sights at a faster pace.

This National Bike Week, discover Cwm Elan by bike.

Covering 70 square miles of reservoirs, historic dams and rugged Welsh landscapes, Cwm Elan offers some of the most memorable cycling routes in Mid Wales.

Whether you prefer quiet road rides, challenging climbs or off-road adventures, there’s a route to suit every rider.

Need a bike? Hire one from the Bike Hub at the Visitor Centre and start exploring.

### Stargaze

Cwm Elan has [International Dark Sky Park status](https://www.elanvalley.org.uk/darkskies), meaning that on clear nights you can see stars, planets and constellations twinkling away with little light pollution. The Elan Valley Astronomy Group holds regular meet-ups at night in the [Elan Valley visitor centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/917601) to educate visitors on the night sky and give people a chance to explore it through telescopes.

### Little adventurers

Cwm Elan is a playground in itself, with plenty of room to run about and discover the interesting wildlife in the woodlands. The Visitor Centre Café caters for children and offers outdoor seating next to a fantastic adventure play area. The well-stocked gift shop has lots of children’s toys, activities and books. Family activities take place during school holidays, including Dam Open Days and workshops such as bug hotel and bird feeder making, bottle rockets and stone painting, so keep an eye on their [calendar of upcoming events](https://elan-valley.co.uk/events/).

## A short drive away...

### Knighton

If proper on-foot adventuring ticks your boxes, [Offa’s Dyke Visitor Centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/518049) in Tref-y-clawdd (Knighton) is worth a visit. It has exhibitions on the history of the area, plus gives access to the Offa’s Dyke Trail. Tref-y-clawdd also has the [Spaceguard Centre](https://www.visitwales.com/product/517514), a National Near Earth Objects Information Centre (NNEOIC) - the UK's only centre addressing the danger of comets and asteroid impact.

### Vale of Rheidol Railway

How’s this for a gentle adventure? One of the [Great Little Trains of Wales](https://www.greatlittletrainsofwales.co.uk/) runs through the Rheidol Valley, from Aberystwyth to Pontarfynach (Devil's Bridge). For over 100 years, the [Vale of Rheidol Railway](https://www.visitwales.com/product/513068) has been treating passengers to the beautiful scenery of the area. Explore more of the Elan Valley by taking the remote, narrow Cwmystwyth road to Pontarfynach to catch the train.

## Before you visit: Elan Valley FAQs

- ### Where is the Elan Valley and how do I get there?











Cwm Elan (The Elan Valley) is in rural Mid Wales, near the town of Rhaeadr Gwy (Rhayader) in Powys. It’s easiest to reach by car, following signposts from Rhayader to the Elan Valley Visitor Centre. Rhayader is also accessible by public transport, with onward options available locally.

- ### What can I do during a visit to the Elan Valley?











Visitors can enjoy walking and cycling routes, wildlife watching and exploring the famous dams and reservoirs. Cwm Elan offers everything from gentle outdoor experiences to longer adventures, alongside opportunities to learn about its history, engineering and dramatic natural landscape.

- ### Are there walking and cycling routes for different abilities?











Yes. Cwm Elan [has a wide range of walking and cycling routes](https://www.visitwales.com/things-do/adventure-and-activities/walking/walking-routes-elan-valley-mid-wales), from short, accessible trails near the Visitor Centre to longer, more challenging routes across the estate. Routes are well signposted, allowing visitors to choose options that suit their time and ability.

- ### Can I visit the Elan Valley with my dog?











Yes. Dogs are welcome throughout Cwm Elan, including on walking routes and at the Visitor Centre café. Because livestock roam freely across the estate, dogs must be kept on leads at all times, and owners are asked to follow local guidance.

- ### Does it cost anything to visit the Elan Valley?











Access to Cwm Elan estate and its walking routes is free. Parking charges apply at some locations, including the Visitor Centre. Additional facilities, such as the café, bike hire and guided activities, are available at an extra cost.
